Solutions

What we do

Every service answers one of three questions about your land. What stands on it now? What has changed since a date that matters? And where should your team go first? Each one is scoped to your route or site, and a person reviews every result before it reaches you.

Request a proposal How we work

Start with the decision in front of you

Three places most projects begin

A resettlement cut-off date, a choice between route options, or a right of way that has to stay clear. Each is a complete service in its own right, and each becomes the baseline for everything that follows.

Resettlement cut-off-date baselines

A dated register of the structures in your project footprint at the cut-off date, to support your census and asset inventory under IFC Performance Standard 5.

Structure counts along alternative alignments or across candidate sites, so land impact is weighed before a route is fixed.

The full service list

Every service, in one list

The individual services behind the solutions above. Every proposal names the services it includes, so your team knows exactly what it is buying.

Encroachment and structure mapping

  • Right-of-way encroachment surveyA register of the structures within the distances you choose from your pipeline, power line, road or railway. Each structure comes with its distance to the line and its coordinates, and each stretch of the route gets an encroachment-density rating.
  • Concession, site and boundary encroachment surveyStructures inside your concession, site or land-use boundary, in a ring around it, or both, mapped and listed so you can see where land is being occupied.
  • Structures in hazard and impact zonesStructures inside the zones you define, such as tailings dam-break inundation areas, blast and exclusion zones, flood lines or safety setbacks, each listed with its location and distance to the source.
  • Route and site option comparisonSide-by-side structure counts along alternative pipeline, line or road alignments, or across candidate sites, so land impact can be weighed before a route is fixed.
  • Area-wide structure mappingA GIS layer of structures across a whole district, concession or imagery survey, ready to load into your own mapping system.
  • Reviewer-led structure mappingWhere automatic detection is not enough, such as dense villages, mixed tree cover or unusual roofs, AfriScan reviewers mark structures by hand on high-resolution imagery.
  • Structure categories and attributesA reviewer tags each structure with what the imagery shows, such as main building, outbuilding, livestock enclosure, under construction or roof type, for resettlement and planning registers.

Change and repeat surveys

  • Change detection between dated surveysNew and removed structures between two or more dated surveys, flagged automatically and confirmed by a reviewer, with before-and-after views of each change.
  • Scheduled re-surveys with change noticesYour route or site re-surveyed on a schedule agreed with you, with an email to your team after each survey saying what has changed and where.
  • Settlement growth trendsHow built-up land has changed year by year around your assets, showing where settlement pressure is growing.
  • Vegetation and land-cover changeMaps of where vegetation has been cleared, has regrown or has changed along servitudes, around plantations and forest estates, and across concessions, compared between dates.
  • Forest-loss and ground-disturbance alertsRegular notices of tree-cover loss and ground disturbance inside or near your estate or concession, drawn from global satellite alert systems and checked by our team.
  • Fire hotspot and burn-scar watchNotices of satellite-detected fire hotspots near your lines, pipelines, plantations and sites, and maps of burnt areas after the fire.
  • All-weather radar change screeningRadar satellite comparisons that show larger ground changes, such as clearing, earthworks and new large buildings, even under rainy-season cloud.
  • Rehabilitation and revegetation trackingProgress of revegetation on rehabilitated mine land, closed borrow pits and restored servitudes, tracked between dates.
  • Construction and earthworks progressDated drone orthophotos and elevation models compared side by side, with maps of where ground has been cut or filled between visits.
  • Boundary and perimeter changeNew structures, cleared ground and new tracks at your boundaries between dates, with fence lines and gates checked by a reviewer on drone imagery.

Detection of specific features

  • Track and access-route mappingNew tracks and access roads into your concession, across your right of way or around your site, mapped between dates.
  • Structure detector tuned to your imageryA building detector tuned to your own drone or satellite imagery and to local building styles, checked on part of your area before it is used on the rest.
  • Custom object detectionDetection of the objects that matter on your land, trained on examples from your own imagery and reported alongside structures in your GIS files and reports.
  • Artisanal mining and excavation mappingPits, disturbed ground, spoil heaps and water-filled excavations mapped inside and around your mining right or concession, with new sites flagged between dates.
  • Excavation and third-party works on rights of wayFresh digging, spoil heaps, trenches and earthworks on or near your pipeline or cable right of way, flagged between surveys so your field teams know where to check.
  • Tanks, containers and stored materialsAn inventory of tanks, containers, stockpiles and laydown areas on your sites and along your corridors, compared between dates.
  • Plant and equipment on siteHeavy equipment, such as excavators and trucks, visible at construction sites, laydown yards and unexplained earthworks, recorded on each survey date.
  • Describe-what-to-find searchTell us in words what to look for, and we search your imagery for it, with every result checked by a reviewer.

Terrain, water and hazard screening

  • Terrain, slope and erosion screeningSteep, erosion-prone and drainage-crossing stretches of your route or site highlighted from elevation data, with drone elevation models for detail where flown.
  • Flood-exposure screeningStructures, route segments and sites in historically flooded, low-lying or river-crossing areas, highlighted for planning and emergency preparedness.
  • Post-event flood and damage mappingAfter a cyclone or flood, a map of the flooded area and a reviewer's before-and-after check of structures and assets along your route or site.
  • Vegetation height in servitudesWhere tall vegetation stands inside your power-line or pipeline servitude, mapped from drone elevation models and open canopy-height data.

Land and social baselines

  • Resettlement cut-off-date baselineA dated record of the structures in the project footprint at the cut-off date, with imagery, coordinates and IDs, to support your census and asset inventory under IFC Performance Standard 5.
  • Evidence packs for legal and community processesDated imagery, structure registers and maps packaged with file fingerprints and an independent timestamp, so you can show what was on the ground and when.
  • Imagery history and land due diligenceThe documented history of a parcel, route or site from archived satellite imagery and open datasets: what was built, cleared or changed, and roughly when.
  • Location check for grievances and claimsFor a single point or claim, a sheet of every dated image covering it, so your team can see what was there on each date.
  • Household and population estimatesEstimated households and people from structure counts, for mini-grid sizing, service planning, consultation planning and health or census microplanning.
  • Land-use and land-cover baselineA baseline map of built-up land, cropland, bare ground, water and tree cover around your project, combined with our structure register.

Drone and imagery

  • Drone orthophoto and elevation surveyA georeferenced orthophoto, surface and terrain elevation models, a point cloud, a 3D model and a processing quality report from a drone survey of your site or corridor, subject to the permits and authorisations each job requires.
  • Drone checks of flagged areasSatellite screening narrows the search, then drone flights over the flagged stretches capture the detail your team needs, subject to the permits each job requires.
  • Stockpile and earthworks volumesVolumes of stockpiles, spoil heaps, borrow pits and cut-and-fill areas calculated from drone elevation models.
  • Analysis of your own imagerySend the drone orthophotos or satellite scenes you already have, and we run the same structure, change and corridor analysis on them.
  • Very-high-resolution satellite imagery sourcingDated, very-high-resolution satellite scenes of your area sourced from commercial archives, used in your analysis and delivered as imagery.
  • New satellite capture of your siteA new very-high-resolution satellite capture of your site or corridor, requested from commercial operators for when archive imagery is too old. The capture date depends on satellite availability and weather.

Reports and delivery

  • PDF reports in English or PortugueseClear PDF reports with maps, route tables, a photo of each structure and a coordinate register, in English or Portuguese.
  • GIS deliverablesGeoPackage, GeoJSON, KMZ and Shapefile layers that open in QGIS, ArcGIS and Google Earth.
  • Interactive map fileA self-contained interactive map of your results that your team can open in a web browser, including in the field.

What we never offer

No tracking or counting of people or vehicles, no night imagery, no leak, theft or pipeline-integrity detection, no cadastral or statutory surveys, and no client portal or logins. Results are delivered as reports and files, and a person reviews every result before delivery.

Frequently asked questions

Which service should we start with?

Usually a baseline right-of-way or boundary survey. It gives you the register every later service compares against. If a decision is pending, such as a resettlement cut-off date or a choice between route options, start with that instead.

Can we combine several services in one survey?

Yes, and most projects do. A right-of-way baseline often includes excavation and track mapping, a cut-off-date record usually comes with household estimates and an evidence pack, and drone checks follow wherever satellite screening flags a stretch. The proposal lists every service it includes.

Are drone services available in every country?

Drone surveys are available subject to the permits and authorisations each job requires, which differ by country and sometimes by site. Satellite-based services need no drone flight and are available in Mozambique, South Africa and Nigeria.

Can you detect things other than buildings?

Yes, where they are visible at the imagery’s resolution: excavations, tracks, tanks and containers, heavy plant on work sites and similar objects. Detection tuned to your imagery is checked on part of your area before it runs on the rest. We never detect or track people.

How are results delivered?

As files your teams already use. A PDF report in English or Portuguese, GIS layers in GeoPackage, GeoJSON, KMZ and Shapefile, and an interactive map file that opens in a browser. There is nothing to log in to.
